subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel A-Level English Literature specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: Analysis of theme and character in drama transfers to prose, where the comparative unit adds the skill of reading two texts together
The comparative method built on prose pairs is reapplied to set poems and their contexts
Close attention to dramatic verse and imagery sharpens the analysis of poetic language and form
Comparative essay-writing on prose is the core skill the independent NEA comparison demands
Studying Shakespeare and other drama supplies texts and critical approaches for the independently chosen coursework comparison
The analytical and contextual skills from poetry support the wide reading required for the NEA
